_note: AI-drafted Call to Worship — pending Wilson's curation.

registers.label: Spare
lines: My God, my God, why have you forsaken me?
He was wounded for our transgressions.
Like a lamb led to the slaughter, he did not open his mouth.
By his wounds we are healed.
It is finished; he bowed his head and gave up his spirit.
By his wounds we are healed.
Through the torn curtain, let us draw near.
By his wounds we are healed. Amen.

registers.label: Immersive
lines: Stand at the foot of the cross in the middle of the day, and watch the sky go dark, and hear him cry, why have you forsaken me.
By his wounds we are healed.
He was despised, a man of sorrows, acquainted with grief; we held him of no account, and he carried what was ours.
By his wounds we are healed.
Like a lamb led to the slaughter, like a sheep silent before the shearers, he did not open his mouth.
By his wounds we are healed.
The crown of thorns, the nails, the spear, the vinegar; and then the words, it is finished, and his head bowed down.
By his wounds we are healed.
By his blood a new and living way is opened through the curtain; come, let us draw near and worship.
By his wounds we are healed. Amen.
